newsitem.title: UK: Enterprise Oil quashes takeover rumours.
newsitem.headline: Enterprise Oil quashes takeover rumours.

text.p: Enterprise Oil Plc quashed recent stock market rumours as it said on Thursday it was not planning any bids for either Monument Oil and Gas Plc or British-Borneo Petroleum Syndicate.
Takeover talk this week had focused on those two companies in particular.
"We have no intent to bid for Monument," Enterprise chief executive Pierre Jungels told Reuters in an interview.
He added British-Borneo was operating in a specific niche of the offshore oil exploration sector, which was of no interest to Enterprise, which earlier reported a 40 percent '96 profit rise.

"I say good luck to them, but that is not the route we want to take in the Gulf of Mexico," Jungels said. "British-Borneo has found a niche which is quite extraordinary in terms of technology, but that is not what we are looking for."
British-Borneo initially fell over 100 pence, but then recouped most losses to trade down 27-1/2p at 1,395 by 0843 GMT.
Monument was named in a press report over the weekend as a possible target for Enterprise, which was said to be ready to make substantial acquisitions this year.
The company had been frequently touted as being interested to launch a bid for British-Borneo, which has promising operations in the Gulf of Mexico where Enterprise recently made inroads.
Speaking in general, Jungels played down any expectations that Enterprise was preparing itself for a major acquisition after he took over the helm on January 1.

"Chances of an acquisition are no more, no less than in any other year," Jungels said, who was an executive at British Gas before taking over the chief executive post from Graham Hearne, who now acts solely as chairman.
